AI01.answer: Turn on your camera grid and step back until the whole building fits. Hold the phone level at chest height so vertical lines stay straight. Place the building on one grid line rather than dead centre, leave a little sky above the roof, and tap the building to set focus before shooting.

AI04.answer: Toss the small wooden jack six to ten metres away. Players then throw their metal boules to land as close to it as possible; the team farther away keeps throwing until it is closer or runs out. When all boules are thrown, the closer team scores a point for each boule nearer than the opponent's best.

AI06.answer: Try the Mikan drill: stand under the hoop, step with your left foot and shoot a soft right-handed layup off the backboard, catch the ball, then step with your right foot and shoot left-handed on the other side. Keep alternating for a minute, aiming at the square on the backboard.

AI09.answer: Pick a rope that reaches your armpits when you stand on its middle. Hold the handles at hip height with elbows close to your body, and turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms. Make small, low jumps on the balls of your feet, starting with single jumps before building a steady rhythm.

AI13.answer: Start with a power grip: tuck your four fingers under the rim against its inside edge, with your thumb on top of the disc. For shorter, controlled throws, try a fan grip with your fingers spread under the disc. Keep the disc flat, pull it straight across your chest and follow through towards the target.

AI19.answer: Stand facing the net with your non-hitting foot slightly forward. Hold the ball at waist height in your non-hitting hand. Swing your hitting arm back and then forward like a pendulum, striking the ball just below centre with the heel of your hand or a closed fist, and follow through towards your target.

AI22.answer: Put each type of seed in its own small paper envelope, fold the top over twice and tape it shut. Write the plant name, variety and year collected on the front. Carry the envelopes upright in a small box or tin so they stay dry and don't get crushed.

AI26.answer: Use algebraic notation: the piece letter (K, Q, R, B, N; none for pawns) and the square it lands on, such as Nf3 or e4. Add x for a capture (Bxe5), + for check and O-O for castling. If two identical pieces could reach the same square, add the starting file or rank, like Nbd2.

AI29.answer: Hold the magnifying glass close to your eye, then move your face and the glass together towards the bark until the detail comes into focus, without touching the tree. Look for patterns in the cracks, moss, lichens and tiny insects, and compare a smooth patch with a rough one.

AI31.answer: Use a forehand grip: hold the racket as if shaking hands with the handle, with a V between your thumb and index finger on the top edge. Keep the grip relaxed. For an easy low serve, hold the shuttle by its feathers, drop it gently and swing from below the waist to push it just over the net.

AI35.answer: Two teams score by catching the disc in the opposing end zone. You can't run while holding the disc and have about ten seconds to pass it. If a pass is dropped, intercepted or goes out of bounds, the other team takes over. There is no contact, and players call their own fouls.

AI39.answer: A chess clock has two timers, one for each player. After you make your move, press the button on your side: this stops your clock and starts your opponent's. Press it with the same hand that moved the piece. If your time runs out before the game ends, you lose, so watch your remaining minutes.
